page: Microsoft Azure D2ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dadv6 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to a single physical core with hyper-threading enabled, running at a base clock speed of 3.7 GHz. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes a bundled 118 GB NVMe SSD for local storage. No GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included in this configuration.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance is limited by the dual-vCPU configuration, resulting in weak multi-core scores in stress-ng and Geekbench. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with read-only small block cached bandwidth scoring in the bottom 10% and large block read-only bandwidth in the bottom 25%. Write bandwidth and single-threaded compression/decompression tasks perform at average levels.

The D2ads_v6 offers a cost-effective entry point for workloads requiring dedicated AMD EPYC compute resources and local NVMe storage without the overhead of larger instance sizes. Due to its low memory bandwidth and weak multi-core scaling, it is poorly suited for database operations, heavy multi-threaded compiling, or large language model inference. It is best utilized for lightweight general-purpose workloads, single-threaded tasks, basic text processing, and small-scale web serving.
